fact: Opinion piece in Novo Jornal says that in June 2026 Starlink was still in the licensing process in Angola, with regulators yet to approve full commercial deployment, and that the licensing process begun in 2024 remains ongoing.

Eutelsat Group announced it secured a definitive 15-year licence to operate its OneWeb LEO connectivity services in Angola, the first LEO operator licensed there, after inaugurating a Luanda ground station; the document gives no licence date, so as_of is the publication date.

The Secretary of State for Telecommunications said on 15 April 2025 that Starlink's licensing process with regulator INACOM was still under way with nothing further to report, so Starlink was not yet licensed.

Agence Ecofin reports Angola is among 16 countries where Starlink's availability map shows 'Starting in 2026', meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending; no launch date given, so Starlink is not on sale in Angola (as_of is the article date).
Eutelsat OneWeb secured a 15-year operating licence in Angola in July 2025, and later partnered with Paratus Group to extend LEO satellite connectivity including Angola.

Starlink is not launched in Angola: the minister says negotiation is in its final phase, but the process has dragged over two years, launch is rescheduled to 2026, and it is unclear where the licensing process with INACOM stands (as_of is the article date).
Angola is listed among countries where Starlink is announced as available from 2026 but no licence has been granted (as_of is the article date).

INACOM, the regulator, authorised the Luena-based startup NomaTech (Weza Tchisseque Tchamy) to install infrastructure and sell internet access over the ANGOSAT-2 satellite network to individuals, institutions and businesses; the document gives no licence date, so as_of is the 2 July 2026 publication date.
Angop reports that Eutelsat is currently the only low-earth-orbit satellite operator licensed in Angola, with a local ground station and point of presence.

Mercury signed a multiyear agreement with Eutelsat to supply low-earth-orbit satellite connectivity in Angola to businesses, public institutions, telecom operators and offshore clients; the document gives no subscriber figures or consumer sale.
